title: Private Control Plane Canary Traffic Slicing Playbook and Version Compatibility Matrix
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Automate safe, auditable canary upgrades for the Private (VPC) control plane by combining Terraform workspace isolation, targeted traffic-slicing, and an explicit compatibility matrix for API contracts/CRDs. This ticket defines the playbook, the IaC requirements, acceptance tests, and operational gating criteria. Scope: - Build Terraform modules and workspace conventions to deploy staged control-plane replicas (canaries) in a subset of customer VPCs. - Add automated traffic-slicing (percentage-based request routing) and shadowing paths for verification. - Define compatibility matrix for control-plane API surface, CRD versions, and operator versions; codify allowed version skews and migration steps. - Create health-check hooks and SLO-based gates (latency, error rate, reconciliation lag) that gate promotion. Out of scope: full-service-data migrations and tenant schema changes that require offline migration windows.

acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules deployed to canary workspace without affecting production remote-state
Traffic slicing can be adjusted declaratively (0.1% - 50%) and changes are reflected in routing telemetry
Compatibility matrix covers all exposed APIs and CRDs with explicit skew tolerances and migration instructions
Automated health gates (latency, error rate, reconciliation lag) are implemented and block promotion when thresholds exceeded
Rollback path validated with 2 simulated failures and recorded in runbook
implementation_notes: Use Terraform provider pinning and lockfiles to ensure deterministic plans across CI runs
Routing: envoy weighted clusters + header-based routing for tenant isolation; shadow traffic via x-envoy-original-token header
Health checks: build small agent to report controlplane-metrics (api_p95, api_error_rate, operator_reconcile_lag) to Prometheus; implement alert rules and Grafana dashboard
Compatibility checks: generate CRD diffs with `kube-compat` tool and fail CI when breaking changes detected unless migration step provided
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Terraform state drift between canary and prod -> Mitigation: nightly drift detection job and plan diff reviewer approval
Risk: Silent API regressions under low-volume canary -> Mitigation: shadow 100% of mirrored traffic to canary for 1 hour before promotion
Risk: Customer telemetry leakage in canary cohort -> Mitigation: scrub PII in synthetic tests and ensure audit logs are gated to runbook owners
Risk: Operator CRD incompatibility -> Mitigation: staged operator rollout with CRD conversion webhooks and preflight checks
